faqs.question: What is an MBA in Product Management?
faqs.answer: An MBA in Product Management is a specialised business degree that focuses on the strategy, development, marketing, and life cycle of products especially in tech, consumer goods, and services. It trains you to become a Product Manager (PM) which is the person who decides what gets built, why, and how. You will get to learn the following: Product development strategy Customer discovery and UX Business model innovation Agile, Scrum, and Kanban Go-to-market (GTM) strategies Cross-functional leadership In short: it is the CEO of the product role with both strategic and execution responsibilities.

faqs.question: Who should pursue an MBA in Product Management?
faqs.answer: MBA in Product Management is perfect for you if you check all the pointers below: You are passionate about technology or innovation You want to build and launch meaningful products You enjoy solving customer problems You love working at the intersection of business, design, and tech You dream of working in startups, tech giants, or building your own venture It is ideal for engineers, designers, marketers, or business graduates who want to step into product leadership roles.

faqs.question: What is a Product Portfolio and why do I need one?
faqs.answer: A Product Portfolio is a showcase of your work, case studies or product thinking which is  crucial for cracking PM roles and interviews, especially as a fresher. Your portfolio may include: Case study on improving a known app (e.g., Uber, Zomato) A product you built (app, website, or feature mockup) Go to market (GTM) strategy for a fictional product Product teardown of a competitor A deck explaining how you'd solve a real world user problem Below are the examples of some tools to build it: Notion (best for organized portfolios) Google Slides / Docs Figma (for product mockups) Pro tip: Link your portfolio in your resume and LinkedIn!

faqs.question: What is the role of a Product Manager?
faqs.answer: Product managers provide the product's direction and success. Their responsibilities are broad, but they typically include the following, irrespective of the size of the company. Defining Product Vision and Strategy : They set the long-term vision and strategy for the product, aligning it with company goals. Prioritising Features : Deciding which features to build and the order of development based on customer needs and business priorities. Product Roadmapping : Creating and maintaining a product roadmap, outlining the planned progression of the product over time. Stakeholder Management : Collaborating with various stakeholders, including customers, team members, and executives, to ensure alignment and buy-in. Read in-depth about managing stakeholders . Market Analysis : Conducting market research to understand trends, analyse competitors , and market needs. In different industries and company sizes, these responsibilities can vary. In startups, a product manager might handle a broader range of tasks, while in larger companies, they might specialize more, focusing on specific aspects like user experience or market analysis.

questions.question_text: Is NMAT mock test released officially?

answers.answer_text: GMAC provides official NMAT mock tests on its website. Two free mock tests, each containing 108 questions with exam structure similar to the actual test is provided online. Candidates can alson pay to purchase NMAT mock tests.

questions.question_text: Will GMAC release NMAT question papers?

answers.answer_text: No. GMAC does not release NMAT question papers. Candidates can find NMAT sample papers issued by different coaching institutes that may have a similar test structure as that of NMAT exam.

questions.question_text: What is the NMAT admit card release date?

answers.answer_text: GMAC does not release NMAT admit card on a specified date for all applicants. NMAT admit card is issued to the candidates based on their scheduled exam date. Candidates can find NMAT Admit card 6-7 days before their exam date.

questions.question_text: How to find NMAT admit card?

answers.answer_text: Candidates can find NMAT admit card inside the login dashboard. GMAC issues NMAT admit card to all candidates who complete the online registration process.

questions.question_text: How difficult is JIPMAT exam compared to IPMAT?

answers.answer_text: Generally, JIPMAT is considered easier than IPMAT Indore and IPMAT Rohtak. Past test-takers have specifically noted that the Quantitative Aptitude and Verbal Ability sections are relatively easy.

questions.question_text: Is it a good idea to give multiple MBA entrance exams like CAT CMAT XAT MAT?
questions.answer_text: Yes, giving multiple MBA entrance exams like CAT, CMAT, XAT, and MAT is generally a good idea. Most of the syllabus overlaps, so your preparation works across exams, and it reduces the risk of depending on just one test.Different exams open doors to different colleges. For example, CAT is needed for IIMs, while exams like CMAT, MAT, or NMAT are accepted by many private B-schools. Colleges such as Athena School of Management also consider multiple exams and focus on the overall profile, so having more scores gives you flexibility.Overall, multiple exams simply mean more options and backup choices, which is always helpful.

questions.question_text: Is quality of MBA education declining?
questions.answer_text: I don't think the quality of MBA education is declining overall, but it's becoming very uneven. A lot more colleges have opened in the last few years, so the quality really depends on the institute you choose.Top and mid-tier B-schools still maintain good faculty, internships and placement support. But some smaller colleges don't update their curriculum or offer enough industry exposure, which makes the experience feel outdated.So it's not that MBA quality is falling everywhere — it's just important to pick a college that focuses on practical learning, internships and industry linkages rather than just classroom teaching.
